title: 最新方法！国内免费无限制，使用Claude Code！
text:
If you wish to use Claude Code, there are two main paths:
either subscribe to their official paid plans,
or manually link up with some third party API services.
Either way, you have to pay up.
but lately, I found a way for you all to use
Claude Code freely, with no limits!
not only can it write code and copy,
but you can also use its image and video
generation models endlessly!
In this video, I’ll guide you through
how to do it step by step.
Without further ado, let’s dive in!
First off, I want to introduce the three tools
we’ll be covering today.
First up, our star for today:
Claude Code—widely deemed
one of the most potent AI Agent tools out there.
It's a simple,
one click install—just follow the official docs'
single command.
I won't elaborate.
Tool number two is Agnes AI.
It’s a free AI model platform.
But don’t mistake it for some wrapper or relay—its text,
image, and video
models are ALL one hundred percent homegrown!
In fact, it rivals top tier models from OpenAI and Google.
Its key feature is that
it makes this whole suite of multi modal APIs
fully available, free of charge—not just the text model,
but image and video generation models, too.
And not some capped trial—no limits, no expiry,
letting you use it freely at zero cost!
You might wonder: free? How many folks would even use it?
In fact, within the first week
after it went free on the first of june,
its text model saw over one trillion calls,
and image generation topped two million images.
and video generation hit two million seconds.
While I can’t quite grasp their strategy, for us users,
this is a real, tangible perk!
The third tool is called cc switch.
It’s a free, open
source project—you can think of it as an API switcher.
Which backend Claude Code connects to, what key to use,
the API address, and which model to run—all of that
is managed right here by it.
Once set up, to switch which one you use,
just click it—and you’re switched!
Today, we’ll use it to swap
Claude Code’s backend over to Agnes AI.
So, to sum up: Claude Code does the work,
Agnes AI provides the free models,
and cc switch links them both together.
Once we grasp how these three tools relate, let’s get started!
First, let’s grab Agnes’s free API Key.
Open Agnes’s API platform,
click “API key” in the left menu bar,
then hit “Create new key”—just give that key any name you like.
Then, open CC Switch’s top toolbar
and first, switch over to the “Claude CLI” tab—
that one’s meant for configuring Claude Code.
Then, click the plus sign in the top right corner
to add a new provider;
pick “Claude Provider,” then select “Custom Provider.”
Next, fill in the info.
For the first field, API Key,
paste in that key you just copied from the Agnes platform.
The second field is the request URL—its job is to forward
Claude Code’s
requests to Agnes’s gateway.
Next, for API Format, choose “OpenAI Chat Completions”;
leave the Auth Field as default.
Click 'Fetch Model List'—if models appear,
you're connected to Agnes.
Then, create a model map,
mapping all these models to Agnes
two point oh Flash—this way,
no matter which one Claude Code calls,
it will in fact run on Agnes’s free model.
Once all is confirmed, click Save,
and the Agnes entry will pop up in the provider list.
But just configuring it
isn’t enough—we also need cc switch
to actually forward those requests.
Click Settings up top left, head to Route Config,
enable Local Routing, then flip on that Claude route switch.
Lastly, head back to the provider list,
find Agnes, and click Enable;
thereafter, all of Claude Code’s requests
will pass through cc switch
and get routed to Agnes’s free gateway.
We can type the Claude command in the terminal,
send a “hi”, and see it has replied successfully!
And with that,
the whole setup is done—but the video’s not over yet!
since I aim not just to show you how to set this up,
but also to show you just how well this free model performs.
First, let’s test the text model—I’ll use a real world task
from my own work.
Here’s some of my own video ops
data—over one hundred entries,
spanning several platforms.
In Claude Code,
I had it call Agnes’s Agnes two point oh Flash.
“ Based on this data, craft an ops review dashboard for me.”
And look at what came out—
—charts, filters, details—all there; the layout’s clean,
totally ready for daily reviews.
Then, I had it
upgrade that into a business collab landing page
I could send straight to brands.
This version is complete too:
data snapshots, key works,
and cooperation methods—all looking very professional.
Ready to use.
From a plain data table, to a review ready dashboard,
and then to a page for landing business deals—
all powered by the free Agnes model.
For a free model to yield such results—
I’d say that’s quite impressive!
Next up, let’s test the image model and see how well it draws!
Since Claude Code only hooks up to text models,
I crafted a special skill to call
Agnes’s image generating model.
Using it is super simple: just within the chat box,
ask Claude Code to generate an image based on a prompt,
and it’ll automatically call up this skill.
and it’ll spit the image right into your project
dir!
Now, let’s see the results!
First, I tested its text to image prowess,
having it generate a thirty five millimeters film,
direct flash style portrait
based on this prompt.
And here’s the result!
that thirty five millimeters film texture,
plus those highlights from the flash hitting the face—
you can even see the skin texture and pores, lending it
such realism under that flash.
The whole vibe is that street sports style—
and the results are quite good!
If you were to use those paid, closed source image gen models,
one decent shot could cost you a few cents.
Plus, with AI image gen,
doing it just once might not yield perfect results—
you tend to rerun the same prompt over and over,
and those costs really add up!
but with Agnes, it’s ALL zero cost—sample away,
try as you please, not a single dime spent!
Same results—once you had to pay for them,
but now they’re free—and THAT’s the best part!
Next, I tested out
Agnes’s image to image prowess—meaning,
I fed it a reference pic
and had it create anew based on that.
Let’s see the results!
What pops out is a standard headshot—waist up shot,
natural expression,
and a very genuine smile.
Most importantly, the face stays the same,
but the clothes, background, and lighting all get swapped out!
This face preserving outfit swap
ability is handy—one casual photo
and a prompt
create a professional headshot for resumes,
LinkedIn, or personal sites.
So, the image to image work is highly polished, too.
Okay! Now, let’s check out
its video generation skills—I used this prompt
to create a short clip of a female singer singing.
Let’s see the result.
The shot is a close up
of a red haired female singer—her curls,
the highlights in the backlight—all are crystal clear.
But what I find most remarkable
is how the expression evolves.
At first, she’s calm, eyes closed, gearing up;
then, she slowly gets into it,
opens her mouth and starts to sing,
until her brows furrow slightly,
and she becomes wholly lost in the emotion.
Her hand on the mic, her mouth movements,
the rhythm of her breathing—it all flows together,
sans that stiff, “AI fake” vibe.
Of course, this model acts up now and then—for instance,
I used this prompt
to make a video of a beauty on a night street shoot.
At first glance,
the lead lady and night scene look quite real.
but take a closer look,
and you’ll spot a weird yet fascinating thing:
the passerby on her left suddenly splits into two,
as if one was cloned out of thin air.
But the main subject—i.e., the woman herself—is quite stable,
and the parts that should be sharp are sharp.
When this happens, just have a laugh and reroll a few times!
After all, for a model that’s fully free and unlimited,
letting you sample away
until you’re happy—well, that experience itself
is pretty rare!
Okay! And that wraps up today’s freebie guide!
If this video helped you out,
remember to Triple Combo and follow me—see you next time!
